title: PAWP-TTS: Phoneme-Aware Weight Programming for Compact Bilingual English-Nepali Speech Synthesis
why_wsp: Inspection-guided, zero-training closed-form (ROME-style rank-one) edits to a trained 1.5M-parameter TTS model, designed and run with the assistance of an AI research agent, evaluated against matched random and same-parameter gradient controls; most of the paper is a compact TTS system.
editor: ROME-whitened / null-space rank-one closed-form edits; experiments 'designed and run with the assistance of an AI research agent (Gemini 4 Neon)'
target: PAWP-1.5M (1,490,390 parameters) ConvNeXt1D + iSTFT TTS model
interface: closed form (rank-one ROME-style updates, single bias shift)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "duration_predictor.proj.weight (96 params = 0.0064% of model)"; Nepali residual edit "(6,144 params = 0.41%)"; 1-parameter duration bias shift (Sec 5.2-5.3)

headline_results.quote: A ROME-whitened Rank-1 update achieved 27:1 surgical selectivity on untouched test data (<sp> +1.001 frames vs. phonemes +0.037 frames)

headline_results.claim: Pause edit not better than random control
headline_results.quote: the edit did not beat a matched random-96 control on overall NE PER (4.93%, p = 0.177 vs. 4.84%, p = 0.004)
reduced target confusion but degraded overall PER (NE +1.22%, EN +1.75%)
90.3% (65/72) of the targeted /b/ → /w/ errors were a v2 cache-label artifact on va words

headline_results.claim: 1-parameter bias shift gives only significant gain
Language-residual edit zero collateral, no gain
headline_results.quote: achieved exact 0.000% English collateral by construction and 0.00% Nepali PER collateral (5.036% → 5.026%, p = 0.495)

headline_results.claim: Label fix larger than any edit

baselines_and_controls: Matched-norm random edits at same location; same-parameter gradient fine-tuning; 1-parameter global duration-bias calibration; validation-only selection with one-shot test; native human recordings to validate edit targets.
runs_and_variance: Edits evaluated once on untouched test (n = 300 NE + 300 EN) with paired-bootstrap 95% CIs; TTS architecture comparisons over three seeds (42, 101, 202) with mean ± std.
verification: Paired bootstrap 95% CIs and p-values; 'independent AI agents audited the methodology and results'. No formal verification.
limitations_stated: Small held-out ASR set (n = 30/30/9) with single recognizer; lexicon not audited against native gold set; single speaker; teacher-generated target voice; latency per-chunk only. WSP-specific: edits gave no accuracy gain beyond controls.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 weight-space programming blog [1]
notes_for_survey: Applies WSP-style inspect-localize-edit-verify to a small TTS model with matched random and gradient controls; edits were selective but did not beat controls, and two apparent edit targets were label or phonology artifacts. A one-parameter bias calibration explained the random-edit gain.
